nodes.title: Choose construct and controls
nodes.body: Human liver cancer research currently lacks in vitro models that faithfully recapitulate the pathophysiology of the original tumour.

nodes.title: Run assays against controls
nodes.body: We recently described a novel, near-physiological organoid culture system, where primary human healthy liver cells form long-term expanding organoids that retain liver tissue function and genetic stability.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: PLC-derived organoids are amenable for biomarker identification and drug screening testing and lead to the identification of the ERK inhibitor SCH772984 as a potential therapeutic agent for primary liver cancer.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: We thus demonstrate the wide-ranging biomedical utilities of PLC-derived organoid models in furthering the understanding of liver cancer biology and in developing personalized medicine approaches for the disease.
